A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUPE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments across 42 tasks, first-goal-time measurements, ablations and data-quality tests, including Figure 3, Table 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results across the same 42 tasks, including learning curves, first-goal-time measurements and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The trajectory-VAE skills, optimistic reward and skill labeling, fixed-horizon execution, and high-level RLPD training with offline and online data remain unchanged. HILP w/ Offline Data is renamed SUPE (HILP), with the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 42 tasks. The change from seven to eight domains counts cube-single and cube-double separately; both were already evaluated in v2. The additional dataset-quality and corruption scenarios in Appendices H–J also match.

E2.justification: The Online baseline's Visual AntMaze result in v2 Figure 3 is absent from v3's corresponding comparison. Its AntMaze and Kitchen results remain in Appendix H. The other comparator changes primarily rename retained methods, including HILP w/ Offline Data as SUPE (HILP).

E3.justification: Appendix C changes the documented ICVF initialization for trajectory skills/SUPE: v2 replaces only the RND encoder with ICVF weights, whereas v3 specifies both RND and critic encoders. However, v3 Appendix E retains the RND-only description. This establishes a reported setting revision, but not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same ICVF and KL ablations, RND-coefficient and horizon sweeps, exploration-coverage analyses, and data-quality/corruption tests remain. No new analysis question or test condition is established; changes to statistical summaries and displays are assessed separately.

E5.justification: v2 specifies means and standard errors for appendix plots; v3 specifies IQMs and 95% stratified-bootstrap confidence intervals throughout, substantially changing statistical summarization. Table 3 newly specifies a one-sided t-test. Figure 17 changes the AntSoccer seed count from four to eight, although v2 already states eight elsewhere, so an actual increase in runs is unestablished.

E6.justification: Reported curves and some findings change with the revised summaries. Appendix I.2 changes SUPE's matched-or-outperformed count from 11/15 to 12/15 manipulation tasks, and the HILP variant's Scene advantages from four tasks to three. Table 3's numerical entries are identical. The aggregation changes preclude interpreting these revisions as demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, VAE objective, skill-labeling equations and optimistic-reward losses are retained. Defining the dataset explicitly as trajectories clarifies the sequential input already required in v2. There are no new substantive derivations, assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains using unlabeled trajectories both to pretrain skills and to train their online composition, enabling faster exploration and learning. Explicitly stating 42 tasks and renaming the HILP variant do not expand the contribution already presented in v2.

C2.justification: Appendix J.2 removes the explanation that reduced offline data weakens learned skills and narrows SUPE's advantage over ExPLORe. The substantive limitations concerning frozen skills, RND on high-dimensional observations and poor skills extracted from noisy exploratory data remain.

D1.justification: v3 deletes Table 2, losing important online-agent settings such as update-to-data ratios, actor delay, network sizes and entropy parameters. Appendix A loses per-experiment runtime estimates, and direct baseline implementation links are removed. v3 newly specifies 256-dimensional RND features, while retaining the VAE table and SUPE code link.

R1.justification: The options discussion and bibliography drop Daniel et al. (2016b), Probabilistic inference for determining options in reinforcement learning. This is distinct from the retained Hierarchical relative entropy policy search reference. The broader positioning relative to skill discovery, hierarchical RL and ExPLORe remains stable.

P1.justification: There is substantial paragraph-level rewriting across the abstract, related work, method exposition and experimental narrative. Algorithm 1 is reorganized into explicit stages, baseline and domain terminology is standardized, implementation descriptions are reordered, and a brief Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws Figure 1 and incorporates the aggregate learning curve previously in Figure 3. The domain illustration moves to appendix Figure 5. Plot grids, legends, colors and markers are extensively redesigned, the ICVF figure becomes two panels, and Table 2 disappears.

improvement.justification: Clearer organization and more explicit statistical reporting are useful, but v3 removes essential online-training settings from Table 2 and introduces conflicting ICVF initialization descriptions in Appendices C and E. These reproducibility losses outweigh the presentation gains, although the central method and empirical support remain intact.
